cells.tense: The thinking is gathered now and the direction is clear to you.
cells.act: let the inner compass decide the small case
cells.ask: The next small call this week, hand it to the private sense of what's right, then act on it before you've justified it to yourself.
cells.core:
You can pull a dozen loose threads of thought into one direction and then actually move that way. Not a surge — a line. When something needs fair deciding, the answer shows up before the reasoning does, and the reasoning trails behind it a while later. That quiet read is what keeps the momentum pointed right, and it works best when you don't run it past anyone first.

So let it take a small case this week. Something minor, nobody watching, no explanation owed to a single soul. Let the inner sense of what's right make the call, then move on it. Justification can arrive afterward. What you're practicing is acting on that read without checking it against someone else first, because the habit of checking is what turns a straight line into a wait.
cells.sheetLine: You know what's fair before the reasons show up.
cells.verb: Gathering scattered thinking into one line of action
cells.place: Where energy gets aimed at a goal and keeps going

cells.tense: The strategy keeps being rewritten ahead of a future that won't hold still.
cells.act: find the rhythm and stay in it
cells.ask: Choose a pace you could hold across a whole season, and keep to it through the next stretch of work without re-plotting it.
cells.core:
The gathering has turned into gathering more — every plan rebuilt before the last one has run. The momentum is still there. It keeps getting aimed at the next version instead of being allowed to arrive somewhere. And the bracing costs feeling: the direction and the genuine engagement have come apart, so the push is doing work that desire used to do.

Find a rhythm and stay in it. Not a speed that suits one day — one that suits a season. Pick it for a single stretch of work and don't re-plan it partway through. If the pace is right, the pull comes back, and you'll feel the difference between moving on purpose and moving because standing still got uncomfortable. A season is a real test. A day is not.

cells.tense: The direction was set a long time ago and nobody is walking it now.
cells.act: sit with what the heart already knows
cells.ask: For twenty minutes, sit with the sense of where you meant to be headed — no deciding, no fixing — and don't touch a thing.
cells.core:
Where energy used to get aimed at something and stay aimed, the aiming has stopped. Not a decision — a drift. Plans still exist, and there's a direction on some shelf or other, but the walking of it isn't happening, and the calendar moves on without you. What's left is feeling that hasn't been attended to, while the days go by.

So sit with it. Twenty minutes with the sense of where you meant to be headed — not to plan it, not to fix it, just to let it be there. Nothing here asks for effort from you. That's the point. Do it a few times before you decide anything about the direction. The answer isn't needed yet.

cells.tense: The steering is happening — the route was chosen and the car is moving — and the account of it is that things just lined up.
cells.act: let the gladness go out to the room
cells.ask: When something good lands, say it out loud to whoever is nearby, right then, instead of filing it as the natural result.
cells.core:
Pulling the pieces together and pointing the whole thing somewhere is what's happening here, right now. Ask about it and the reply is that things just lined up, that anyone would have done it, that the direction was obvious. The route keeps getting set and the setting keeps getting described as the outcome.

Something good will land soon — a piece that fits, a plan that holds, a thing finished. Let the gladness go out to the room when it does. Say it out loud, to whoever is near you, the moment it happens. Not a summary later, not a private nod. It's a small thing and it marks what you actually did. The people around it already know who steered. This is you finding out.
